error.defines_both: This template defines both "{first}" and "{second}". A template can only define one of card, badge, element or row.
error.defines_nothing: You must define one card, badge, element, or row in the template
error.strict_one: This variable has no value: {which}. The card is set to strict, so it refuses rather than rendering the brackets.
error.strict_many: These variables have no value: {which}. The card is set to strict, so it refuses rather than rendering the brackets.
error.for_each_not_card: for_each needs a template that defines a card. "{template}" defines a {kind}, which Home Assistant gives one slot - put what you want repeated inside a card template instead.
error.missing_template: Missing template object in your config
error.no_lovelace: Could not retrieve the lovelace configuration.
error.template_missing: The template "{template}" doesn't exist in decluttering_templates or in a custom:decluttering-template card.
error.template_missing_anywhere: The template "{template}" doesn't exist in decluttering_templates, in a custom:decluttering-template card, or on any dashboard listed in decluttering_templates_from.
error.cycle_self: The template "{first}" uses itself ({path}), which would never finish. A template cannot contain a card that uses it.
error.cycle_loop: These templates use each other in a loop ({path}), which would never finish. One of them has to stop using the next.
error.too_deep: Templates are nested more than {max} deep ({start} → …), which is deeper than anything is meant to go. Check whether a template ends up using itself.
error.variables_shape: Variables must be a list of key and value pairs, or a mapping of them
card.debug_builds_from: Debug: what this card builds from "{template}".
editor.no_such_template: No template exists with this name
editor.extras_helper: Anything this template does not describe. Example: - variable_name: value
editor.for_each_helper: One copy of the template per item. Example: - entity: light.hall, name: Hall
editor.for_each_from_label: Repeat for each thing Home Assistant knows about
editor.for_each_from_helper: One copy per entity or area, kept up to date. Example: domain: light, area: Kitchen
editor.gap_helper: Pixels. Leave it out for the spacing Home Assistant uses everywhere else
editor.empty_helper: A card to render when the repeat produces no copies. Example: type: markdown, content: Nothing here
editor.columns_helper: How many copies sit side by side. One stacks them vertically
editor.min_column_width_helper: Pixels. Drops a column rather than going narrower, so the card suits a phone too
editor.fit_helper: Get out of the way if a card that sizes itself comes out spread across the row
editor.result_hint: The {kind} this card builds, with every variable put in. Anything still written as [[name]] is a variable nothing gave a value to.
editor.result_error: Could not work out the result: {error}
editor.source_borrowed: This template is borrowed from another dashboard, so it is edited there.
editor.matches_none: Nothing matches this right now, so the card renders nothing{but}. Check the domain, area or label against what Home Assistant actually has.
editor.matches_hint: What it matches is worked out again whenever Home Assistant's registry changes, so this list is what the card would build now.
editor.fit_hides_style: This card is set to get out of the way, so it has no box of its own - and the styles here that paint on it have nothing to paint on. Style the card inside it, or set this back to keeping its own box.
editor.required_one: This template needs a variable you have not set: {names}.
editor.required_many: This template needs variables you have not set: {names}.
editor.optional_one: This template uses a variable with no value and no default: {names}.
editor.optional_many: This template uses variables with no value and no default: {names}.
editor.unused_one: This variable is set here but never used by the template: {names}.
editor.unused_many: These variables are set here but never used by the template: {names}.
template_editor.description_helper: What this template is for, shown to whoever uses it
template_editor.declarations_helper: Describe a variable and its editor shows the right control. Example: - name: entity, selector: {entity: {}}
template_editor.declarations_shape: The declarations must be a list, each entry naming one variable
template_editor.declared_unused_one: This variable is declared but never used in the template: {names}.
template_editor.declared_unused_many: These variables are declared but never used in the template: {names}.
template_editor.duplicated_one: This variable has a default in both places; the declaration is the one that counts: {names}.
template_editor.duplicated_many: These variables have a default in both places; the declaration is the one that counts: {names}.
template_editor.contradictory_one: This variable is marked required but has a default, so it can never be unset: {names}.
template_editor.contradictory_many: These variables are marked required but have a default, so they can never be unset: {names}.
template_editor.order_hint: The order these appear in is the order every card using the template shows them in.
template_editor.in_use_one: One card or template uses this. Changing it changes that one, and deleting this card leaves it pointing at a template that is not there.
template_editor.in_use_many: {total} cards and templates use this. Changing it changes them all, and deleting this card leaves them pointing at a template that is not there.
template_editor.suggest_nothing: Nothing here looks like it varies between copies. Entities, names, titles and icons are what get offered, and this card either has none or they are variables already.
template_editor.suggest_confirm_one: This will rewrite the card to use {names}, and declare it with the value it has now. Press again to go ahead.
template_editor.suggest_confirm_many: This will rewrite the card to use {names}, and declare them with the value they have now. Press again to go ahead.
template_editor.usages_unreadable: The dashboard configuration could not be read, so uses cannot be counted here.
template_editor.usages_none: Nothing on this dashboard uses "{name}" yet. Cards on other dashboards are not counted here, even ones that borrow this dashboard's templates.
template_editor.usages_one: One card uses "{name}" on this dashboard. Cards on other dashboards are not counted.
template_editor.usages_many: {total} cards use "{name}" on this dashboard. Cards on other dashboards are not counted.
template_editor.used_by_template: This template is used by another template: {names}. Changing it changes that one too.
template_editor.used_by_templates: This template is used by other templates: {names}. Changing it changes those too.
share.export_hint: Copy this and send it to someone else, or paste it into another dashboard.
share.copy_failed: Could not copy - select the text above instead
share.import_hint: Paste a template someone shared with you. It will replace the one you are editing.
share.import_clash: This dashboard already has a template called "{name}". Importing will give you two templates with the same name, and only one of them will be used. Press Import again to go ahead.
share.import_not_yaml: This is not valid YAML, so it cannot be read.
share.uses_other_templates: Uses these other templates, which are not included here: {names}
share.import_not_a_template: This does not look like a template: it should be a block of YAML keys and values.
share.import_no_name: This template has no name: it needs a "template:" line.
share.import_defines_nothing: This template defines nothing: it needs one of "card:", "badge:", "row:" or "element:".
share.import_defines_both: This template defines both "{first}" and "{second}": it can only define one of them.
share.library_hint: Worked examples of the shapes people build most. Installing one adds it to this view as its own template card, leaving the one you are editing alone.
tools.rename_hint: Changes the name here and in every card on this dashboard that uses it. Cards on other dashboards are not touched, even ones that borrow this dashboard's templates.
tools.rename_confirm: This renames "{from}" to "{to}"{rewrites}, and saves the dashboard straight away. Press again to go ahead.
tools.cannot_save_here: This dashboard cannot be saved from here, so it cannot be changed here either.
tools.cannot_rename_here: This dashboard cannot be saved from here, so it cannot be renamed here either.
tools.name_taken: A template called "{name}" already exists on this dashboard.
tools.duplicate_hint: Adds a copy of this template to this view under a new name, and saves the dashboard. The copy is yours to change; nothing using this one is touched.
tools.duplicate_confirm: This adds "{to}" to this view as a copy of "{name}", and saves the dashboard straight away. Press again to go ahead.
tools.modernise_header: Move off the original card's names
tools.modernise_hint_one: One card on this dashboard still uses the original decluttering-card type names. It works, because this card answers to both - but it would stop working the day the original is installed alongside it.
tools.modernise_hint_many: {count} cards on this dashboard still use the original decluttering-card type names. They work, because this card answers to both - but they would stop working the day the original is installed alongside it.
tools.modernise_confirm_one: This rewrites that card to this card's own names, and saves the dashboard straight away. Press again to go ahead.
tools.modernise_confirm_many: This rewrites all {count} of them to this card's own names, and saves the dashboard straight away. Press again to go ahead.
library.room_light_tile.summary: A tile per light, with the light named after itself.
library.room_summary.summary: A heading per area, listing the lights in it. Uses grouping.
library.sensor_line.summary: An Entities row showing one sensor with its area.
library.status_badge.summary: A badge that only appears when something needs attention.
library.counted_grid.summary: A numbered grid of anything, showing "3 of 12".
warn.gave_up: decluttering-card-plus: gave up substituting variables after {passes} passes. Check whether a variable refers to itself.
warn.refused: decluttering-card-plus: left {which} in the card rather than substituting. {why}
warn.refused_transform: A transform only shapes text, so it needs a scalar value - applying one to a mapping or a list would garble its JSON. Give the variable a scalar value, or drop the transform.
warn.refused_resolver: A resolver reads its value as an entity id and asks Home Assistant, so it needs one that exists and carries what was asked for.
warn.unresolved: decluttering-card-plus: {whose} uses {which}, which nothing gives a value to, so it is rendered as written. Set it on the card, or give it a default in the template. To write those brackets on purpose, escape it as [[{escape}]].
warn.many_copies: decluttering-card-plus: the template "{template}" is being repeated {count} times on one card. That is a lot to build and a lot to scroll - narrow what it repeats over.
warn.tag_taken: decluttering-card-plus: <{tag}> is already registered by something else, skipping it.
picker.card_description: Reuse multiple times the same card configuration with variables to declutter your config.
picker.badge_description: Instantiate a template whose content is a badge.
picker.template_description: Define a reusable template for decluttering cards to instantiate.
picker.legacy_card_description: Compatibility alias for existing custom:decluttering-card configurations.
picker.legacy_template_description: Compatibility alias for existing custom:decluttering-template configurations.
